nodes.label: Worker Bundle Size Check (3072 KiB budget)
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare's 3MiB free-plan script-size rejection was only discovered at the real wrangler deploy step, after build already ran (e.g. @react-pdf/renderer's PDFKit dependency silently pushed the script over the limit, three separate times). A dry-run deploy reports the same gzipped size without touching the live Worker, so this fails fast with a clear message. Budget is set to the real 3072 KiB hard limit (not a conservative number) because the app is already at ~3052 KiB gzipped with only ~20 KiB headroom; a tighter budget would fail CI on every deploy even though nothing is broken. Real headroom must come from removing bundle weight (the @react-pdf/renderer -> jsPDF swap bought back ~900 KiB once already).

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL Secret Format Correction Step
nodes.rationale: `wrangler secret put <key>` has no `--value` flag (confirmed via a real CI failure: 'Unknown argument: value'); the documented mechanism is reading the value from stdin via a shell pipe, which cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3's `command:` input can't express, so wrangler is called directly here instead. This step exists specifically because DATABASE_URL is the one secret with a previously-undocumented, non-obvious correct format (direct endpoint, no -pooler, no channel_binding); all other live secrets are left untouched by this workflow.

nodes.label: Verify Live Health After Deploy Step
nodes.rationale: Every prior deploy through this pipeline was manually checked with a one-off curl against /api/health afterward; this step makes that check part of the pipeline instead of relying on a human to remember, with retries since a fresh Worker version can take a moment to propagate.
